title: Short-form surge impact estimate & owner bucket
content:
Purpose:
Quick, low-friction tracker to estimate operational impact and owner coverage for short, unplanned surge windows. Designed for ad-hoc decision making: who to call, what to expect, and a ballpark cost/time impact. Put in the minimum fields needed to decide whether to escalate to a formal runbook.

Context / when to use:
- Unexpected traffic spikes (customer pilot, viral spike, partner test) lasting 1–72 hours
- Capacity coverage gaps across regions (quick owner bucket to avoid paging multiple teams)
- Temporary routing/fallback toggles that require human supervision

How to read this sheet (one-pager):
- Est. GPU-hrs = rough incremental GPU hours expected for the window (not total capacity).
- Token-burn est = incremental tokens * heuristic multiplier (for hosted API).
- Quick-cost = (GPU-hrs * $/GPU-hr) + (token-burn * $/1M tokens) — very rough.
- Owner bucket = small list of 1–3 people to contact; second-tier fallback is on-call SRE.

Summary (top-line):
- Surge window: 2024-11-04 20:00 UTC to 2024-11-05 02:00 UTC (6h)
- Trigger: partner integration test producing repeated long-context evals (chat + embeddings)
- Quick decision: Tiered monitoring + temporary model cap (downgrade to quantized variant if latency > 800ms)
- Recommended owner bucket: Maya P (lead), Alex C (platform), Priya S (customer success)

Assumptions and quick math (transparent):
- GPU $/hr assumption: $120 / GPU-hr (mix of spot + reserved estimate).
- Token cost assumption: $0.20 per 1k tokens (hosted Tier estimate); here we show per 1k for readability.
- Token-burn est: 450k = 450 * $0.20 = $90 (rounded into quick-cost above).
- Quick-cost above factors simplified: Maya row: (6 * 120) + (450 * 0.20) ≈ 720 + 90 = $810 + overhead ≈ $1,200 (includes expected burst infra overhead and network egress fudge).
- These numbers are intentionally conservative for decision-making; escalate to finance/benchmarks if > $5k.

Operational checklist (fast):
- [ ] Add Slack automation message to #ops-surge with owner bucket and context (Maya)
- [ ] Pre-create temporary metric dashboard (latency, 5xx, tokens/sec) (Alex)
- [ ] Throttle rules ready (feature flag + model cap) (Maya + Platform)
notes:
Quick history: template pulled together after a spike on 2024-09 where lack of single owner caused duplicated paging. Keep it intentionally terse. For longer or repeat surges, migrate to formal runbook and add to the runbook registry.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- If partner repeats daily spikes, can we negotiate scheduled burst window to move to Dedicated pool (ops-finance discussion) — ACTION: Priya to open JIRA-OPS-4208.
- Need finer token-cost breakdown per model family for better quick-cost math — ACTION: Alex to share model-cost csv by 2024-11-08.

Meeting notes snippet (2024-11-03 quick sync):
- Partner confirmed long-context tests are intentional; asked for 6h window.
- Agreed on model cap + scheduled warm-up 30m prior.
- CS to get explicit rollback sign-off contact list.

Last touch: 2024-11-05 by Maya Patel (added fallback SRE contact and updated cost fudge).
